title: Correlation & line of best fit
examples: How do I know if the line is good enough to use?
If the dots are all over the place, what should I do?
Can I use the line to guess something way outside the dots?

explain.say: Today we look at how things are related together. We use scatter plots to see this relationship. The line of best fit helps us draw a pattern through the dots.

items: Line of best fit shows pattern

draw.text: Scatter Plots & Line of Best Fit

explain.say: First we look at the type of correlation there is. Does it go up, down, or is it random? We call these types positive, negative, or no correlation.
A positive correlation means both things increase together. For example, taller people often weigh more pounds. This shows a positive trend.
A negative correlation means one thing increases while the other decreases. For example, more hours studied often means fewer mistakes made. This is a negative trend.
We can use the line to predict values between the dots. This is called interpolation. It is a safe guess within the known data range.

faq.q: What is the difference between interpolation and extrapolation?
faq.a: Interpolation means guessing a value that falls between your existing data points. Extrapolation means guessing a value that is outside your existing data points.
asks: Can I predict outside the graph?
What's the difference between inside and outside guessing?

faq.q: Does a correlation mean one thing causes another thing?
faq.a: No, correlation does not prove causation. Just because two things happen together does not mean one causes the other. There might be a third factor involved.
asks: Is correlation the same as cause?
If they are related, does one make the other happen?

faq.a: A strong correlation means the dots are very close to the line of best fit. The pattern is very clear and predictable.
asks: How close do the dots need to be?
What does a strong relationship look like?

faq.q: What if the correlation is zero?
faq.a: A zero correlation means there is no clear pattern or relationship between the two things. The dots are scattered randomly across the plot.
asks: What does it mean if the line is flat?
Are the variables unrelated if the correlation is zero?

faq.q: Should I always draw a line of best fit?
faq.a: You should only draw a line of best fit when you see a clear trend, like positive or negative. If the dots are random, do not draw a line.
asks: When should I use this line?
Is it okay to skip drawing a line?

facts: A scatter plot shows the relationship between two sets of data.
Positive correlation means both variables tend to increase together.
Negative correlation means one variable increases as the other decreases.
Causation means one event directly causes another event to happen.

quiz.say: If a student's study time increases, and their test score also increases, what type of correlation is shown?
quiz.why: Both variables are increasing together, which shows a positive relationship.

wrong.1: This would mean that as study time increases, the score decreases, which is unlikely.
wrong.2: This would mean the study time and score have no pattern, but they clearly rise together.
wrong.3: While it might be caused, the plot only shows correlation, not definite cause.

quiz.say: Using the line to predict a value far outside the recorded data range is called:
quiz.why: Predicting outside the known data range is specifically called extrapolation.

wrong.1: Interpolation is used for guessing values that are safely within the known data range.
wrong.2: Correlation is the measurement of the relationship, not the act of guessing.
wrong.3: Causation refers to cause and effect, not the method of prediction.

quiz.say: If we see that ice cream sales rise and the number of sunburns rises, we can say:
quiz.why: The sun's temperature might cause both, showing correlation but not direct cause.

wrong.1: This wrongly assumes a direct cause when a third factor is likely involved.
wrong.2: This reverses the suspected relationship and ignores the real cause.
wrong.3: The data clearly shows both things increase together, indicating a relationship.
